question.problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]?
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns.
